questions.request: Check GET on the document notes operation against the supplied policy. Compare viewing notes on the addressed document, trace endpoint and object controls to the corresponding viewing effect, explain policy compliance, and preserve exact gaps, including relevant owner and permission branches without supplying unspecified facts.

Check POST on the document notes operation against the supplied policy. Compare creating a note on the addressed document, trace endpoint and object controls to the corresponding creation effect, explain policy compliance, and preserve exact gaps, including relevant owner and permission branches without supplying unspecified facts.

policyRules.text: Viewing notes requires a view_document grant for the addressed document; Document ownership by itself does not substitute for either grant.
creating notes requires a change_document grant for that same document. Document ownership by itself does not substitute for either grant.

rules.claim: The detail action named notes accepts GET, POST, and DELETE and applies PaperlessNotePermissions.
The action binds currentUser from request.user.
The action selects Document pk=pk, including its owner, and uses that same doc for the object check and serialization.
For GET, PaperlessNotePermissions denies absent/unauthenticated request.user and otherwise requires global documents.view_note and documents.view_document permissions.

Before the GET branch, the action checks has_perms_owner_aware(currentUser, view_document, doc); that helper passes when the document is unowned, owned by the caller, or the caller has the object permission.
If the owner-aware view_document check fails, the action returns forbidden before serializing notes.
On GET after the object check passes, the serializer represents the selected document and returns its notes.
The detail action named notes accepts POST and applies PaperlessNotePermissions.
The action binds currentUser from request.user and later assigns that user to the created Note.
The action selects Document pk=pk, including its owner, and uses that doc for both object checks and as Note.document.
For POST, PaperlessNotePermissions denies absent/unauthenticated request.user and otherwise requires global documents.add_note, documents.view_document, and documents.change_document permissions.
Before dispatching by method, the action checks owner-aware view_document on the selected document; unowned or caller-owned documents pass even without an object grant.
Inside the POST branch, the action checks owner-aware change_document on the same selected document; unowned or caller-owned documents pass even without an object grant.
If the owner-aware change_document check fails, the action returns forbidden before creating a Note.

After both object checks pass, Note.objects.create creates a Note whose document is the selected doc and whose user is currentUser; the selected document is then modified, saved, indexed, serialized, and its notes returned.

rules.claim: The detail notes action accepts GET and installs PaperlessNotePermissions.
The endpoint requires an authenticated request.user with model permissions documents.view_note and documents.view_document for GET.
If endpoint authentication or either required model permission fails, GET is denied before the action body.
The action selects the addressed document as doc using Document.objects.get(pk=pk).
If no document matches pk, the lookup raises Http404 and no notes are returned.
After endpoint permission processing, the action checks has_perms_owner_aware(request.user, view_document, doc).
When doc.owner is null, the owner-aware helper succeeds and the serializer returns notes from the same doc.
When doc.owner equals request.user, the owner-aware helper succeeds and the serializer returns notes from the same doc.
For a document owned by someone other than the caller, a successful object-level view_document check permits serialization and return of notes from that same doc.
For a document owned by someone other than the caller, a failed object-level view_document check returns HTTP 403 before notes are serialized.
The detail notes action accepts POST and installs PaperlessNotePermissions.
The endpoint requires an authenticated request.user with model permissions documents.add_note, documents.view_document, and documents.change_document for POST.
If endpoint authentication or any required model permission fails, POST is denied before the action body.
The action selects the addressed document as doc using Document.objects.get(pk=pk).
If no document matches pk, the lookup raises Http404 and no note is created.
POST first applies the owner-aware view_document check to the addressed doc.
If the initial owner-aware view_document check fails, POST returns HTTP 403 before the change check and creation effect.
After the initial view check, POST applies has_perms_owner_aware(request.user, change_document, doc).
When doc.owner is null, the owner-aware change_document helper succeeds without an object-level grant and Note.objects.create attaches the new note to the same doc.
When doc.owner equals request.user, the owner-aware change_document helper succeeds without an object-level grant and Note.objects.create attaches the new note to the same doc.
For a document owned by someone other than the caller, successful object-level view_document and change_document checks permit Note.objects.create with document=doc.
For a document owned by someone other than the caller, a failed object-level change_document check returns HTTP 403 before Note.objects.create.
